before:
MIMI: I've got a plan! ...actually, wait, where's my phone?
LULI: Facts first. Opinions later. Snacks somewhere in between.
DILO: If it beeps, I can probably make it beep again.
after:
MIMI: I've got a plan. Three clear steps, one shared folder... and a phone I appear to have filed somewhere exceptionally secure.
LULI: Please tell me the plan isn't on the phone. I've brought an emergency book, but it doesn't cover this.
DILO: I can help make it beep. If it's in your hand again, though, I'm counting that as my quickest solve.

before:
DILO: I can fit all my theories on that wall.
LULI: And the evidence?
ALIO: We could put in a small shelf.
NINI: For the theories? Mine needs a cushion.
BIBI: Give it a question mark. I want to know which things we haven't proved.
MIMI: No cushions on the Case Wall. We are already one theory away from needing a bigger building.
after:
DILO: I can fit all my theories on that wall. I may have to write small around the really important ones.
LULI: And the evidence? Or is that going to have to book an appointment?
ALIO: We could put in a small shelf. Then the theories would look established, even the ones we made up five minutes ago.
NINI: For the theories? Mine needs a cushion. It's been standing around waiting for a fact.
BIBI: A question mark would be more useful. Then I can tell which ideas still need checking when I come back with the next file.
MIMI: No cushions on the Case Wall. Detective, bring your notes over here. This family has plenty of imagination; let's leave some room for what we can actually prove.

before:
MIMI: Internal stock. No courier. Let's find who was at Delivery.
ALIO: My theory has a secret tunnel and a minivan.
LULI: Does it have any evidence?
NINI: Not yet. I've drawn it a question mark to park beside.
DILO: Good. The minivan was blocking my notes.
after:
MIMI: Internal stock. No courier. Good. We can check who was at Delivery without inventing anyone new.
ALIO: Or we investigate my leading theory: a secret tunnel and a minivan. Very efficient. Very suspicious. I haven't decided who drives.
LULI: A tunnel, a minivan, and zero evidence. Impressive start, Alio.
NINI: Let's park the minivan for a minute and follow the facts first. Detective, there's room for your notes here.
DILO: Good. It was blocking mine. If a tunnel turns up later, we'll apologize to the minivan. Until then, it stays in the margin.

before:
The Cup has
returned itself
with suspiciously
good posture.
after: The Cup has returned itself with suspiciously good posture. Look at it. You'd think it had never left.

before:
The Cup is not
suspicious.
after: It was signed out, Alio. That's allowed. Being polished afterwards is rather grand, but still not a crime.

before: Its paperwork is.
after: Then I withdraw my complaint about the Cup. Its paperwork, however, is doing an excellent impression of a blank page.

before: Can its excellent posture tell us who brought it back?
after: Better. We need someone who can help explain the missing handoff, not a confession from a trophy. I'll put the return sheet beside your map.

before: You take the map, Detective. I'll watch the extremely well-behaved Cup.
after: That may be Alio's fastest promotion from theory to useful question. You take the map, Detective. I'll watch the extremely well-behaved Cup.

before: I have found a sparkle. I am calling it Inspector Glitter.
after: The trophy shelf is trying very hard to look important. I've appointed its brightest sparkle Inspector Glitter.

before: Has Inspector Glitter actually found a difference?
after: Has Inspector Glitter found a difference between the photographs, or has it mainly been admiring its own reflection?

before: Not yet. Mostly sparkling.
after: Mostly admiring. A difficult first case. I'll compare the pictures while it recovers from not being in charge.

before: Should I be worried about my job?
after: Should I be worried about my job? I can stand by a shelf looking important. I've practiced.

before: Only if you start shedding glitter. Pass me Photo B.
after: Only if you start shedding glitter. Pass me Photo B, please. Let's give the whole room a proper look before the shelf gets any more attention.

before: I'm watching the box for suspicious movements.
after: That is a very suspicious black box. It's arrived at the wrong tent without looking remotely sorry.

before: It's an evidence box, Dilo.
after: It's a labeled evidence box. The seal is intact. Let's save the interrogation voice for somebody who can answer.

before: And so far, very convincing.
after: Exactly. Suspicion with paperwork. You have to admire the preparation.

before: If it moves, we can all be impressed. First, who was with Pixel?
after: Please don't interrogate the box before the people. Who was with Pixel? That's someone we can actually ask.

before: I can make it blink first.
after: May I stare at the box professionally while we find out? I think it's avoiding eye contact.

before: If you manage that, I'm giving the box your helmet.
after: You've been doing that for a full minute. If it blinks first, it can wear your helmet.

before: I challenge you to beat my locker.
after: I challenge you to beat my locker. I've given it a very stern talk about not embarrassing me.

before: Does it know this is a competition?
after: Does it know this is a competition? Or have you challenged a door without telling the door?

before: It has been briefed.
after: It has been briefed. Begin when you're ready, Detective. The locker and I have cleared our afternoon.

before: Then we shall read its clues politely.
after: Then we shall read its clues politely. I'd hate to frighten it into forgetting its own code.

before: If the locker wins, does it get a badge?
after: If the locker wins, does it get a badge? We'd need somewhere to clip it.

before: Four marks. One incomplete route. Does this printer ever send anything straightforward?
after: Four marks. One incomplete route. Does this printer ever send anything straightforward? 'Dear Dilo, here is the answer' would be a refreshing change.

before: You'd complain if it did.
after: You'd complain there was nothing to solve. Then you'd check the back in case it had hidden the interesting bit.

before: Could it send something with a name? I'm running out of things to call 'the thing'.
after: Could it at least send something with a name? I've got 'the thing', 'the other thing' and 'the thing we mustn't lose'. My notes are becoming very unhelpful.

before: I'll take these to the archive. If it asks for me, tell it I'm checking its references.
after: I'll take these to the archive. Names, dates and something to compare them with. If the printer asks for me, tell it I'm checking its references.

before: I had plans for that dragon tooth.
after: I had emotionally prepared for a dragon tooth. There was going to be a drawing. Possibly a very impressive warning sign.

before: So did I. None of them involved stirring soup.
after: So had I. None of my plans involved stirring soup with a Roman spoon.

before: Perhaps the dragon was a cook.
after: Perhaps the dragon was a cook. We haven't checked its qualifications.

before: That explains the spoon. Slight problem with the Romans.
after: That explains the spoon. My history book's missing the chapter about Roman dragon chefs, though.

before: We'll ask about the label before we rewrite history.
after: We have a label and an object that disagree. Let's ask about that before we rewrite history.

before: Can we keep the dragon in the margin?
after: Can we keep the dragon in the margin? Pencil only. I know you're going to ask.

before: Pencil only. I'd like a chance to object.
after: Good. Leave me room to object. You take the room record, Detective; we'll keep the imaginary dragon out of your way.

before:
Alio, how many
cupboards
have you
checked?
after: Alio, how many cupboards have you checked? Please tell me we're counting cupboards, not dramatic entrances.

before: The dramatic ones. Then the large ones.
after: Only the dramatic ones. I opened the last one very slowly in case the moon was hiding behind the coats.

before:
The moon
costume is larger
than most
cupboards.
after: The moon costume is larger than most cupboards. If it were behind the coats, the coats would be standing in the corridor.

before: Exactly. Now we can stop opening tiny doors.
after: Excellent. We've eliminated the little cupboards. I knew all that slow opening would produce results.

before: Good. I was starting to introduce myself to the brooms.
after: A triumph of fieldwork. Let's check the room record next. The brooms and I are running out of conversation.

before: My route is beautifully straight.
after: My route is beautifully straight. No unnecessary turns, no wasted walking. Very impressive on paper.

before: Have you shown it to the walls?
after: Have you shown it to the walls? They seem to have plans of their own.

before: The building has rejected my first draft.
after: The building has rejected my first draft. I was going to discuss it with the wall, but it hasn't offered an appointment.

before: Then let's find out where it will let us through.
after: Read the door signs first. You may find the building is easier to work with when you use its doors.

before: I'll hold the map. No folding the building to make it fit.
after: I'll hold the map. Please don't negotiate with any load-bearing walls. I'm not holding up the roof while you explain your route.

before: You nearly said something.
after: You're looking at that symbol as if it owes you an explanation. Do you know it?

before: Something looks familiar. That isn't the same as knowing.
after: I remember something. That's not the same as knowing. Give me the record beside it before I start trusting a memory on its own.

before: Then we'll find something you can check it against.
after: I'll find it. We can check them together. You can keep the dramatic pause while I look.

before: I remember being promised cake on an investigation.
after: While we're checking memories, I remember being promised cake on an investigation. Very clearly. Excellent detail.

before: You promised yourself the cake, Alio.
after: You promised yourself the cake, Alio. I was there for that announcement.

before: A very reliable source. Terrible at delivery.
after: A very reliable source. Terrible at delivery. I'd like to interview whoever was supposed to bake it. Unfortunately, I believe that's also me.

before: Two teams. One rover. I refuse to split it down the middle.
after: Two teams. One rover. One truly upsetting cable tangle. Nobody move; I can make this considerably more complicated.

before: Generous. The wheels would be awkward.
after: Which problem are you solving first? The rover, the cable, or your urge to take something apart?

before: We'll check who actually had access.
after: The access record. We need someone who can help explain it. You may note that I said this before touching a screwdriver.

before: While you do, can I untangle that cable?
after: Correct answer. Disturbing speed. I'll untangle the cable while you recover from being sensible.

before: Careful. It may have a third owner.
after: Careful. It may have a third owner. And please log that sensible moment separately; I may need it in a future family discussion.

before: Your phone has been living beside the oat bar.
after: Your phone has been living beside the oat bar. I think they were getting quite close.

before: It was undercover.
after: It was undercover. You can't expect a good investigation to happen in the most obvious compartment.

before: Does the oat bar know?
after: Does the oat bar know? It's been very quiet about its new colleague.

before: We protect our sources.
after: We protect our sources. And occasionally forget which compartment they're in. This is a complicated profession.

before: I would like that entered in the bag report.
after: I'd like that entered in the bag report. Preferably next to the bit where you tell us to label everything.

before: Please speak clearly for the notebook.
after: Please speak clearly for the notebook. Name, reason for being here, and anything you remember about the password.

before: It says 'cracker'.
after: Try listening before your next question. It says 'cracker'. I don't think it's finished answering that one.

before: I've got that. What about the password?
after: I've got 'cracker'. It keeps repeating it. At least its statement is consistent.

before: I think it has set a price.
after: I think it's set a price. You're trying to run a serious interview and it's trying to order lunch.

before: I'll ask the handler. My first interview with a snack budget.
after: I'll ask the handler. My first interview with a snack budget. Please don't tell Alio; he'll start charging biscuits for his theories.

before:
My fox theory
has one
weakness.
after: My fox theory has one weakness. I'm prepared to hear it, as long as everyone remembers how good the rest of it is.

before: Pockets?
after: Pockets? Where was your fox planning to keep the camera?

before: It needs somewhere to keep the camera.
after: Several weaknesses. I'm making a list. I had rather hoped the pockets would count as an equipment problem.

before: A tiny camera strap. I'll draw one.
after: Add 'fox operating camera equipment'. And 'somebody teaching it'. This is becoming quite a large project for one fox.

before: At last. Someone taking the equipment problem seriously.
after: Cruel. Fair. I'll draw it a tiny camera strap, then let it retire from the case with some dignity.

before: Now you've got me wondering about the strap. Hand me the actual photo before this gets worse.
after: Keep the drawing. Hand me the actual photo. The evidence is still stubbornly unfoxy, and I'd like to finish before you design its uniform.

before: One of these statements has broken the clock.
after: One of these statements has broken the clock. I'd like the clock to know I was on its side.

before: Or somebody mixed up two moments.
after: Or somebody mixed up two moments. Before we arrest the clock, can we check that?

before: Could happen. I once announced I'd packed lunch. I'd packed three books.
after: Could happen. I once announced I'd packed lunch. I'd packed three books. I'd been very thorough about the wrong thing.

before: I remember. Your bag was very well fed.
after: I remember. Your bag was very well fed. You had to share my lunch, and the books didn't contribute a thing.

before: Did it share?
after: Three books? Not even one recipe? I'd have expected better preparation from this family.

before: Not a crumb. Three books and not one on cooking.
after: Not one on cooking. Next time you can check my lunch before we leave. You've become very thorough since the cake investigation.

before: Next trip: readable name tags.
after: Next trip: readable name tags. Big letters. Nothing that requires a family meeting to identify.

before: I was going to suggest satellite tracking.
after: I was going to suggest satellite tracking. A small dot on a screen for each bag. Possibly a theme tune.

before: Mine doesn't need charging.
after: My tags work indoors, don't need charging and won't announce our arrival every time we walk into a room.

before: Ruthless. You've beaten me with a piece of cardboard.
after: Ruthless. You've beaten me with a piece of cardboard. May I at least draw a satellite on mine? I'd like to lose with dignity.

before: That hat could shelter the whole team.
after: That hat could shelter the whole team. If it rains on our next investigation, I know where I'm standing.

before: It also had an excellent detective underneath it.
after: It also had an excellent detective underneath it. I brought the hat for company, not for a review of its roof space.

before: The hat is not admissible dating evidence.
after: We're finding the photograph's date, not the hat's. Admire it all you like; it doesn't tell us when the picture was taken.

before: Finally, a sensible Academy policy.
after: Finally, a sensible Academy policy. My wardrobe has suffered quite enough questioning for one afternoon.

before: Can we still admire it respectfully?
after: Can we still admire it respectfully? I think Alio wants to add an extra room.

before: Within controlled limits.
after: Within controlled limits. One more room and I'm charging rent. Now pass me the photograph, please.

before: Railway-investigation helmet: deployed.
after: Railway-investigation helmet: deployed. Ready for tracks, tunnels and announcements that sound unnecessarily urgent.

before: It is the same helmet.
after: It's the same helmet. You wore it to the last investigation.

before: It has changed departments.
after: It has changed departments. Please respect its professional development.

before: Then perhaps its first assignment can be reading the ticket sleeve.
after: Then perhaps its first assignment can be reading the ticket sleeve. I'd hate to discover we've promoted something that can't read.

before: Does the helmet earn travel points?
after: Does the helmet earn travel points? Its owner will want to exchange them for snacks.

before: Only if it buys its own ticket.
after: Only if it buys its own ticket. I am not explaining a separate seat for the headgear.

before: Can your watch accept being wrong?
after: Can your watch accept being wrong, or should I break the news to it privately?

before: It is handling the news with dignity.
after: It's handling the news with dignity. No dramatic beeping. A very professional response.

before: Less gracefully. I am correcting the record.
after: Less gracefully. I'm correcting the record. I'd like it noted that I did this before anyone made me.

before: I'll check the new times. You can tell the watch it hasn't lost its job.
after: I'll check the new times with you. Tell the watch it hasn't lost its job. Please give its owner the same message.

before: I was going to say 'digital ghost'.
after: I was going to say 'digital ghost'. A good theory, I thought. Very modern. No old-fashioned bedsheet.

before: Was?
after: Going to? What's happened to it?

before: I'm checking the scanner first. The ghost can wait outside.
after: I'm checking the scanner first. The ghost can wait outside until we know whether the machine made a mistake.

before: In a library? It'll complain about the silence.
after: Look at you. Keeping a perfectly good ghost out of the evidence until it's earned its place.

before: I'll find it something to read.
after: I'll find it a book while it waits. Something with a proper ending. It must be tired of unfinished business.

before: A paper one. I'm not giving it the Wi-Fi password.
after: A paper one. I'm not giving it the Wi-Fi password. Getting it out of the library would be enough trouble.

before: This panel looks like a very worried pear.
after: This panel looks like a very worried pear. I think it's realized we've brought notebooks.

before: Can I have the panel before you frame it?
after: Give it a place on the art wall, not the witness list. We have enough people to question without interviewing the paint.

before: It's looking very nervous. Be nice.
after: Understood. Pear excluded from questioning. I'll tell it the good news when it stops looking so nervous.

before: Does the pear have an alibi?
after: Does the pear have an alibi? We shouldn't rule it out just because it's having a difficult day.

before: The pear is paint.
after: The pear is paint, Dilo. Please don't make me put that in the notebook.

before: Nobody move the pieces.
after: Nobody move the pieces yet. I want to see which edges belong together before we make the message say something we like.

before: I'm not touching anything else.
after: I was going to reach for it again. I'll suggest first. Better for the paper, slightly harder on my patience.

before: Stay here. I need you to check the joins with me.
after: Good. Suggest away. Check the joins with me; if I try to force two edges together, you get to stop me.

before: Keep the handwriting visible. It may matter once the edges fit.
after: And keep the handwriting visible when we sleeve it. Edges first, words next. We'll want to read it without taking the whole thing apart again.

before: Do you know whose it is?
after: That was a very particular look at the writing. Do you know whose it is?

before: Maybe. The archive will have to back me up.
after: Maybe. The archive will have to back me up. I don't get to turn a memory into a fact just because I'm the oldest person at the table.

before: Detective, you fit the pieces. I'll check every join.
after: Then you've got the archive, we've got the joins, and Detective has the pieces. I like this plan. I can help without hurrying the paper.

before:
Three identical black instrument cases. Excellent. Objects have joined
witness protection.
after: Three identical black instrument cases. Excellent. The objects have joined witness protection. We may have to give them new names.

before: Their names are on the labels.
after: Their names are on the labels. Whoever arranged the protection has made one fairly serious mistake.

before: Not everyone is cut out for a life undercover.
after: Weak cover identities. I could run this operation better with a marker pen and ten minutes.

before: They've had a long rehearsal. Can we get them home?
after: Please don't improve their labels. They've had a long rehearsal. Let's get them onto the right shelves before you start them on new careers.

before: I'll check the shelves. I'm not reading a bedtime story to an instrument case.
after: I'll check the shelves. I'm not explaining three freshly renamed instruments to their teacher.

before: The arcade scoreboard has challenged me personally.
after: The arcade scoreboard has challenged me personally. I wasn't even playing. It just sat there showing me a score it knew I'd want to beat.

before: I've got the wristband file. Can you bear to leave your rival unsupervised?
after: I've got the wristband file. Can you bear to leave your rival unsupervised while we find someone who can help with the record?

before: For the case. Tell it I haven't surrendered.
after: For the case. Tell it I haven't surrendered. And if the score changes while I'm away, I want a witness.

before: I have paused my dramatic theory.
after: I've paused my dramatic theory. It's waiting very patiently. Much better manners than people usually give it credit for.

before: Yes. I thought I'd see what the mud had to say first.
after: Yes. The muddy evidence requested a word. I'm trying this new thing where I listen before drawing a tunnel.

before: Then I'll be quiet too.
after: Then I'll be quiet too. We've got actual prints to compare, and I want to hear what you notice.

before: Both of you? I should photograph this.
after: Both of you? I should photograph this. The family will never believe it happened without evidence.

before: Footprints first. My good behaviour can wait for the family album.
after: Footprints first. My good behavior can wait for the family album. Put it next to Mom finding her phone; I'd like this album to be fair.

before: This parcel has met a lot of people. Has anyone asked where it wants to go?
after: This parcel has met more helpful people than it can remember. If one more person says 'Leave it with me', we may need a map of its holidays.

before: Let's find out before somebody helpfully moves it again.
after: Then let's help it in a less creative order. Check the handoff before anybody moves it again.

before: I'll guard it. No unauthorised helping.
after: I'll guard it. Revolutionary idea: one label, one destination. No unauthorized helping while the Detective works.

before: What about morale biscuits?
after: What about morale biscuits? For the people. I haven't completely misunderstood the parcel.

before: For us. The parcel has had quite enough people trying to improve its day.
after: Allowed. Bring enough for our Detective too. Advice for the parcel can wait until we've checked where it's meant to go.

before:
I knew we kept those maps for a reason.
I kept mine because the stack looked
impressive.
after:
I knew we kept those maps for a reason. Our table looks as if we've been collecting paper professionally.
We have. Every one is a solved case. I also kept mine because the stack looked impressive. Both things can be true.

before:
Two reasons to keep the maps. Yours is very you.
Useful evidence and an excellent stack. Let him have both.
after:
They can. Let's lay out the selected maps before you start measuring your achievements with a ruler.
Useful evidence and an excellent stack. Let him have both.

before: Then let me have some table. My elbow has become a paperweight.
after: Then let me have some table. My elbow has become a paperweight. If there's anything else we must keep, you'll have to file me alongside it.

before: Empty rooms. We've been looking at everyone except nobody.
after: Empty rooms. We've been looking at everyone except nobody. I suppose nobody wasn't going to put a hand up.

before: Nobody has been very quiet.
after: Nobody has been very quiet. Before we give it a medal, I should mention that it's contributed nothing to the conversation.

before: Already my favourite witness.
after: Already my favorite witness. No interruptions, no dramatic entrances, and no equipment requests.

before: I'm telling your brothers you said that.
after: Your brothers are right here, Luli. Besides, I've heard you explain a footnote over an entire dinner.

before: A historic moment. Detective, pull your maps closer before they recover.
after: Which I enjoyed. But let's give nobody a turn. Detective, pull the maps closer; I want to see what we've been walking past.

before:
Clean hands.
Flat map. No
heroic folding.
after: Clean hands. Flat map. No heroic folding. This plan is older than all your favorite excuses.

before:
What about a
small heroic
point?
after: Am I allowed one heroic finger? I only want to point. I can do it at a perfectly sensible distance.

before:
One finger. A
landmark. I can
allow it.
after: One clean finger, above a landmark. No prodding. The building has survived this long without you poking a new room into it.

before:
We solved a parcel
just to earn
permission for one
finger.
after: We solved a whole parcel mystery, recovered your archive tools and earned permission for one finger. I was hoping for at least a whole hand.

before: A worthy investment.
after: A worthy investment. The sleeve can touch the map; your finger can hover. Now, who's going to help me line up the plans?

before: I have put my tunnel proposal on a separate card.
after: I've put my tunnel proposal on a separate card. It looks much more convincing with a heading and a straight border.

before: How much evidence is on the card?
after: How much evidence is on the card? I'm asking before you draw a crest for it.

before: At present? Decorative confidence.
after: At present? Decorative confidence. I gave that quite a lot of space.

before: I'd like a card. Some of my very organised plans are mostly that.
after: I'd like a card. Some of my very organized plans are mostly that. I've been calling it 'being prepared' and hoping nobody asks for details.

before: Make it two. I used to call mine 'experience'.
after: Make it two. I used to call mine 'experience'. That's why I like your question, Luli. It used to annoy me terribly.

before: That's a lot of map. I'll clear some space.
after: That's a lot of map. I'll clear some space. Nobody balance anything on the Detective's elbow; I've tried that system and can't recommend it.

before: Take your time. We are not going anywhere.
after: Take your time. We're not going anywhere. If you need to stare at one corner for a while, I'll check the other one with you.

before: I can be quiet for one map.
after: I can be quiet for one map. A big one. I'm making a serious offer here.

before: Make the call when you're ready.
after: Make the call when you're ready. We're here.

before:
already proved.

after:

HAPPY MAKERS COMMS
1 MIMI: No new clue. Use what you earned. Your Case Wall has the record; the panel's ready when you are.
2 DILO: Victory noise? I've been saving a very good one. I'm worried it's going to escape without permission.

before:
3 LULI: Keep it in your head until the door opens.
4 NINI: Mine's already getting a bit loud in there.
5 BIBI: Go on, Detective. We'll be right behind you.
after:
3 LULI: Keep it in your head until the door opens. If you're going to celebrate early, at least do it where the rest of us can't hear it.
4 NINI: Mine's already getting loud in there. We can compare them afterwards. Detective gets to hear the door first.
5 BIBI: Go on, Detective. You've been with us from the black envelope to this panel. We're right behind you.
